LESSON: WRITING 14.5.1 DESCRIPTIVE WRITING (200 – 240 WORDS)

Grade: SNE  /  physical-impairment / Grade seven
Subject: ENGLISH
Strand: Strand 14
Topic 14.5: Writing 14.5.1 Descriptive Writing (200 – 240 words)
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 2

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Writing 14.5.1 Descriptive Writing (200 – 240 words), part of Strand 14 in SNE  /  physical-impairment / Grade seven ENGLISH.

Key inquiry question: What do you consider when describing something?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

A. identify features of a person, a thing, or a place that can be described

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Writing 14.5.1 Descriptive Writing (200 – 240 words) in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

B. write a descriptive composition on a given subject

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Writing 14.5.1 Descriptive Writing (200 – 240 words) in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

C. underscore the importance of creative writing in communication.  Collaborate with peers to view videos or pictures of people, things or places and list the features of each that can be described in an essay. Learners with postural limitation could be preferentially positioned for enhanced viewing.  Search online and offline for words and expressions that can be used to describe different features like weather emotions, events, and characters. Adjust light intensity when using the digital device for learners with visual difficulties.  Explain the difference between descriptive writing and other forms of writing. Learners with speech difficulties could use alternative communication modes as they share their views. What do you consider when describing something? 144  Allow more time for learners with speech difficulties to express their views.  Read samples of descriptive essays and classify the features that are described and the expressions used in a graphic form for sharing. Learners who may not turn pages to use page- turners or be supported by peers. They could use adapted writing materials or type on appropriate adapted digital devices to record findings.  Create a descriptive composition of between 200 to 240 words on an interesting topic like outdoor sports and display it in a gallery for peer review and revision.

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Writing 14.5.1 Descriptive Writing (200 – 240 words) in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

Follow your teacher’s guidance for group work, discussion, and practice on this topic.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Writing 14.5.1 Descriptive Writing (200 – 240 words) together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
 Communication is developed as the learner writes descriptive composition clearly and correctly.

 Collaboration is promoted as the learner actively engages in peer review of other’s work.

145

Values:
Unity is enhanced as learners engage each other to view videos or pictures of people, things, or places.

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
(PCIs)

Creative thinking is enhanced as the learner composes descriptive texts.

Link to other subjects:

The learner relates the concept of descriptive writing in their writing of similar compositions in Kiswahili.
